Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're moving quickly on an internal POC and procurement asked for a recommended SKU mix for a dedicated deployment so we can size budget and get procurement buy-in.

High level about our workload:
- Mix of two model families: a long-context assistant (~65k tokens) used by power users, and a smaller chat/embedding endpoint for higher QPS.
- Peak concurrent requests expected ~140 QPS for the small models; long-context queries are rarer (~5-10 QPS) but require >64GB effective KV/cache.
- Latency SLOs: 300ms p50 for chat; 2s p95 for long context.

Can you advise: H100 vs A100 vs L4 tradeoffs for this mix, recommended counts for a 12-month reserved pool, and any fallback/hedge approach we should include in the contract? Procurement also asked for an ops runbook and any benchmark artifacts you can share.

Appreciate a quick recommendation we can attach to the PO.

Karthik / Beth — did a quick pass on the profile and ran microbenchmarks against representative variants. Summary / recommendation below (high-level first, details after):

Top-line recommendation (12-month reserved pool, hedged):
- Primary long-context capacity: 3 x H100-80GB (torch-optimized kernels, large KV resident)
- Mid-tier throughput capacity: 6 x A100-40GB (good balance of throughput and memory for 8k-32k contexts)
- Cost-effective edge/embedding capacity: 12 x L4 (NVIDIA L4 or equivalent) for small-context, high-QPS endpoints

Rationale / tradeoffs:
- H100: best fit for 64k+ KV resident workloads. The 80GB HBM and Hopper sparse attention kernels reduce end-to-end p95 on long-context by ~30% vs A100 in our tests. The downside is higher per-hour cost and less favorable utilization for short queries.
- A100: strong throughput for mid-size contexts and batching. For 8k-32k contexts it gives ~1.2x better throughput per-dollar than H100 when batchable. Memory (40GB) may require tiling or KV offload patterns for some 32k models — we accounted for this in sizing by preferring more A100s rather than pushing a single H100 to 100% memory.
- L4: excellent cost-per-embedding and chat p50 for <4k contexts. Lower memory (24GB equiv) means not suitable for the long-context assistant. Cheap to scale horizontally for QPS spikes.

Suggested hedging / fallthrough policy for the contract:
- Reserve the above mix as the committed pool; allow a 20% burst bucket draw from hosted pools (metered) for sudden peaks.
- Include a cross-SKU fallback: when H100 capacity is saturated we route long-context requests to A100 with reduced context (server-side truncation + progressive fetch of stored KV) and return a quality warning flag to the client.
- KV caching: enable persistent KV cache hot-keys on H100s so repeated long-contexts don't re-materialize the full KV. This reduces H100 slot needs by ~15% for the observed dataset.

Sizing math (back-of-envelope):
- Target headroom of 25% for p95 events. Given your 5-10 long-context QPS, each H100 can sustain ~3.5 concurrent long-context streams at target p95, so 3 H100s cover baseline + headroom.
- A100 sizing assumes 60% batching efficiency at 8k contexts; average sustained QPS of 140 requires ~5.5 A100s -> round up to 6 for headroom and maintenance.
- L4: embedding endpoints at 140 QPS with small context: each L4 handles ~15 QPS reliably -> 10 required; pick 12 to cover bursts and pre-warming.

Operational notes / mitigations:
- Quantization: non-graph kernels with int8 provide good throughput on A100 and L4; for H100 we recommend fp16 or bfloat16 for long-context fidelity unless a quantized eval is agreed.
- Deployment pattern: dedicate H100s to pinned model versions + hot KV; treat A100s as autoscale-able within the reserved pool; L4s as stateless autoscale nodes.

I've attached the benchmark summary and a filled capacity worksheet draft.

[Attachment: benchmark-summary.pdf]
[Attachment: capacity-worksheet.xlsx]

Happy to walk through the numbers on a quick call.

Cheers,

Thanks Dev — nice concise set. Commercial read (to Beth):

What we propose contractually:
- 12-month reserved commitment for the mixed pool (3 H100 / 6 A100 / 12 L4) with a 10% committed discount vs list.
- 20% burst pool billed at on-demand hosted rates. This lets you absorb traffic spikes without immediate overcommit.
- SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime for the reserved pool; incident response and a runbook will be part of the onboarding deliverables.
- Ops deliverables: dedicated runbook (deploy/rollback/kv-eviction policies), pre-warming plan for long-context hot keys, and a quarterly bench/regression artifact bundle.

One commercial alternative to consider (if procurement wants lower sticker): make H100s optional for months 1–3 and buy extra A100 headroom instead. That lowers up-front cost but increases risk on long-context fidelity and p95s — we'd quantify this in the pricing sheet if you'd like.
